description: Pumpkin: Minecraft server written in Rust, multithreaded, for Java Edition 26.3 and Bedrock clients. Vanilla world format, plugins in WebAssembly. Under heavy development.
notes: Start it from 'Scoop Apps' > 'Pumpkin (Minecraft server)', or with the command 'pumpkin' in a console.
Both run it in its data folder, so settings, worlds and logs land in
%USERPROFILE%\scoop\persist\Pumpkin\server: they survive updates, and only 'scoop uninstall -p' deletes them.
Stop the server with its 'stop' console command before 'scoop update' or 'scoop uninstall'.
Windows Firewall asks on the first start, and again after each update (the exe moves to a new folder).
Every server listens on port 25565 by default: run one at a time, or change the port in its config.
Under heavy development: some mobs, villagers and redstone are incomplete. No Bukkit, Paper or (Neo)Forge plugins and mods.
Pumpkin sends an anonymous heartbeat to market.pumpkinmc.org every 5 minutes unless turned off.
On a fresh install the manifest writes [telemetry] enabled = false into server\pumpkin.toml;
Pumpkin fills in the other settings on its first start. Set it to true to send the heartbeat.

script: # The server works in the current folder, so the command and the shortcut start it in the persisted 'server' folder.
':: Pumpkin: starts the server; /PAUSE (used by the Scoop Apps shortcut) keeps the window open when it stops.',
':: Written by the gesu Scoop bucket at install time.',
':: Only the shortcut''s own window gets a title; a console that runs the command keeps its title.',
'ECHO Pumpkin: Minecraft Java and Bedrock server written in Rust.',
'ECHO Settings, worlds and logs: persist\Pumpkin\server in your Scoop folder.',
'ECHO Players connect to this computer on port 25565 unless the server config says otherwise.',
'ECHO Type stop and press Enter to stop the server.',
':: The server reads and writes its files in the current folder: the persisted "server" folder.',

post_install: # Pumpkin's anonymous heartbeat (market.pumpkinmc.org, every 5 minutes) is on by default; a fresh install turns it off.
# Pumpkin merges a partial pumpkin.toml with its defaults on start, so one section is enough. An existing file is left alone.
